item.title: Ferrari boss Vasseur frustrated with speculation about future amid Horner links
item.description: Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur described the speculation surrounding his future as frustrating after former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner's comments in an interview fuelled talk of a potential move for the Briton to the Italian team.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Takle
item.content:encoded: Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur described the speculation surrounding his future as frustrating after former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner's comments in an interview fuelled talk of a potential move for the Briton to the Italian team. Horner, who was ousted from Red Bull in July last year, told the Times in an interview published last week that Ferrari would be the only team he would consider joining without an ownership stake on offer. He went on to describe the team as the "dream" and "the sleeping giant of Formula One". "We are not working in the perfect serenity," said Vasseur, who joined as Ferrari team principal in January 2023, after Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix. "For me, firstly, but for everybody in the team, for the media, for 50 percent of the questions (to be) about this, I think it's a bit of a frustrating situation." Horner, who returned to the Formula One paddock at the British Grand Prix a year after his 2025 sacking, ran Red Bull for 20 years. He led the team to eight drivers' world championships -- four with Sebastian Vettel and four with Max Verstappen -- and six constructors' titles. The 52-year-old, married to Spice Girls singer Geri Halliwell, was also in the headlines in 2024 after a female employee accused him of inappropriate behaviour, of which he was cleared after an investigation. Speculation of a return has continued to bubble away since Horner’s ousting, with the Briton linked most notably with Renault-owned Alpine and Silverstone-based Aston Martin. Ferrari, the sport’s oldest and most successful team, who last year signed seven-times world champion Lewis Hamilton alongside their protege Charles Leclerc, haven’t won a title since 2008 when they were crowned constructors’ champions. Kimi Raikkonen remains the last driver to win the drivers’ championship for the team in 2007. The Maranello-based outfit has won two races this year, one apiece for Hamilton and Leclerc, and are second in the overall standings behind dominant Mercedes. But their form has faded with McLaren and Red Bull resurgent. "Mr. Horner is looking for a job -- that everybody knows -- everywhere," said Vasseur. "But what can I do? Just try to do my best to push the team, to rise them to be motivated, focus on what is better today."

item.title: White Sox close season against Rockies, head to unexpected run in playoffs
item.description: The Chicago White Sox were hoping they would wake up Sunday with a chance to do the unthinkable: win the American League Central division two years after losing a record 121 games.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago White Sox were hoping they would wake up Sunday with a chance to do the unthinkable: win the American League Central division two years after losing a record 121 games. But their 9-5 loss on Saturday to the Colorado Rockies, combined with the Cleveland Guardians' 11-5 win over the Kansas City Royals, left the White Sox as the third wild card in the AL. When the White Sox conclude their three-game series with the Rockies on Sunday in Chicago, the game instead will serve as a final tuneup for the playoffs as well as the celebration of a season no one saw coming after three consecutive 100-loss seasons. "Obviously don't get the division, which is disappointing," White Sox manager Will Venable said. "But at the same time it doesn't take away from the fact that we're just so proud of the group and we're in a great spot. Obviously going into the playoffs. We'll get through (Sunday's) game, put our best foot forward and try and win that game and then roll into the playoffs." The playoffs begin Tuesday, and the White Sox will play somewhere in Texas. The opponent is still to be determined on Sunday, but it will be the winner of the AL West -- either the Houston Astros or Texas Rangers. "We want to win the division, of course, but that's not in our hands anymore," third baseman Miguel Vargas said. "Now we have to focus on the next thing." In the rubber game of the current series, Anthony Kay (9-9, 4.53 ERA) is scheduled to pitch for Chicago while Colorado will counter with Kyle Freeland (4-11, 6.48) in a matchup of left-handers. The White Sox (83-78) will finish above .500 for the first time since they won the division with a 93-69 record in 2021. It is also the last time they reached the playoffs. Kay, who has never faced the Rockies (58-103), may be scratched if Venable decides to save him for the best-of-three wild-card series. Freeland's most recent outing came with plenty of emotion for the Denver native. He allowed five runs in three innings on Tuesday in a 7-2 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks in what was possibly his final home game at Coors Field, and Sunday could be his last in a Colorado uniform. The 33-year-old Freeland, whose career began in the Rockies' home opener in 2017, has the most starts (256) and innings pitched (1,391 2/3) in club history and is a free agent after this season. He is the longest-tenured player on the roster and the Rockies' nominee for the Roberto Clemente Award for the fifth consecutive season. The honor goes to the player who best represents the game through community involvement, philanthropy and positive contributions on and off the field. "This guy's meant so much to our organization over the years, and the ultimate pro," manager Warren Schaeffer said. "...The things that he's done for this community and our baseball team over the years and the winning years are priceless. And I just want to thank him publicly for that." Freeland is making his fifth career start against the White Sox, and is 3-0 with a 2.03 ERA in those outings, including a 1-0 record and 1.35 ERA in two road starts. While Freeland battles, it is likely rookie first baseman TJ Rumfield will not play. Rumfield's RBI single in the first inning on Saturday night pushed his average to .300 -- technically .2998 -- and he was taken out before the bottom of the first. "Super happy for TJ. That's an awesome rookie season," teammate Hunter Goodman said. Goodman, who has 41 home runs after hitting two Saturday night, became the first National League catcher to hit 40 or more homers in a season since Javy Lopez did it for the Atlanta Braves in 2003. --Field Level Media

item.title: Still in wild-card race, D-backs stay positive vs. Padres
item.description: The Arizona Diamondbacks enter the final game of the regular season against the host San Diego Padres on Sunday afternoon with an opportunity to make the playoffs, although Arizona will need help.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Arizona Diamondbacks enter the final game of the regular season against the host San Diego Padres on Sunday afternoon with an opportunity to make the playoffs, although Arizona will need help. It is nothing new for the Diamondbacks, who have had their playoff fate determined on the final weekend of the season in each of the past three years. They clinched a playoff berth in Game 161 in 2023 and went on to reach the World Series. They were eliminated on the final day in 2024 and in Game 160 last year, in San Diego. After losing 10-7 to the Padres on Saturday, Arizona (86-75) is one game behind Philadelphia (87-74) in the race for the final wild-card spot in the National League. If the Phillies beat the Tampa Bay Rays on Sunday, Philadelphia will make the playoffs. The Diamondbacks and Phillies split their season series. If the teams wind up tied for the final wild-card spot, Arizona owns the tiebreaker by virtue of a better intradivision record. "We've been fighting to the end of the season," Geraldo Perdomo said after the Diamondbacks had a six-game winning streak halted on Saturday. "We're going to control whatever we can control." San Diego (90-71) on Saturday secured home-field advantage in the NL wild-card series and will host the Chicago Cubs in a best-of-three series that begins Tuesday. Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said his players will attack their challenge in front of them "the same way we do every single day, with great intent, great focus and with designs of winning a baseball game. "That's all we can do." Michael Soroka (9-5, 3.31 ERA) is scheduled to start on Sunday for the D-backs against Randy Vasquez (10-6, 4.01) in a battle of right-handers. With home field in the first round assured, Padres manager Craig Stammen said he will give some of his regulars a day off. "We're going to rest some of our guys, but everybody we are putting in the lineup is a Major League Baseball player and capable of doing anything out on that field, including some spectacular stuff," Stammen said. Manny Machado, who hit his 30th homer of the season and the 399th of his career Saturday, is among those who could get a day off. He has played in 157 games this season. "Sticking with it this year, fighting through a lot of slumps and him not feeling that great, that speaks to the person he is, the character that he has and the baseball player that he is," Stammen said of Machado, who is hitting .216 but leads the team with 90 RBIs. Arizona's Gabriel Moreno will be back in the lineup as the designated hitter, Lovullo said, despite leaving for a pinch hitter in the ninth Saturday after his left hamstring tightened. Moreno was 1-for-3 with an RBI single Saturday and leads the NL with a .31078 batting average. Philadelphia's Luis Arraez is hitting .31040. No Diamondbacks player has won a batting title. Soroka arguably made his most efficient start of the season when the Diamondbacks needed it most his last outing Tuesday, when he gave up two runs (one earned) on two hits in seven innings of a 7-2 victory at Colorado. He struck out nine, one short of his season high, and retired 14 of the last 16 batters he faced. "He's been very consistent," Lovullo said. "He's been very dependable. Once he takes the mound and starts to attack, he's got really good stuff that's going to allow him to go into different quadrants of the strike zone with different types of pitches. That's a credit to his arsenal and the hard work he puts in." Soroka, who has missed time with glute and shoulder injuries this season, has not faced the Padres this season and is 2-0 with an 0.90 ERA in four career appearances against them. Fernando Tatis Jr. is 3-for-7 against him, while Machado is 0-for-8 with three strikeouts. Vasquez scattered three hits over two scoreless innings in a no-decision against the Miami Marlins on Sept. 19. San Diego won 7-6 in 10 innings. Vasquez allowed two hits over six scoreless innings in a 9-4 victory over Arizona on Aug. 4. He is 1-0 with a 3.03 ERA in seven career appearances (five starts) vs. the Diamondbacks. --Field Level Media

item.content:encoded: Pakistan's Finance Minister discussed potential US Export-Import Bank financing for Boeing aircraft for privatised PIA (PIAHa.PSX) , refinery upgrades and Reko Diq, a copper and gold mining project in southwestern Balochistan, his adviser Khurram Schehzad said in a post on X on Sunday. Schehzad said the government was helping PIA access financing and suppliers, but was not buying aircraft and had announced no sovereign guarantee or taxpayer-funded loan. US EXIM could secure financing against the aircraft and assess the airline or lessee's creditworthiness, he said, so a sovereign guarantee was not automatic.

item.title: AL Central champion Guardians coast into finale seeking sweep of Royals
item.description: A late-season surge has sent the Cleveland Guardians to their third straight American League Central title, and a potential opportunity to end the regular season in care-free fashion.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: A late-season surge has sent the Cleveland Guardians to their third straight American League Central title, and a potential opportunity to end the regular season in care-free fashion. However, the Guardians still have a chance to sweep their final regular-season series from the host Kansas City Royals on Sunday. Cleveland (85-76) has won three straight, nine of its last 10 contests and is 24-10 since Aug. 20. On Saturday, the Guardians got behind 3-0 after one inning, but received two homers apiece from Patrick Bailey and Brayan Rocchio and nine extra-base hits overall to rally for an 11-5 victory. That win, coupled with the second-place Chicago White Sox's 9-6 home loss to Colorado on Saturday, secured the Central title for Cleveland, which will receive a bye into the division round of the postseason. The Guardians have won 14 division crowns since 1995. "We came into this series having a mission," Cleveland's Chase DeLauter told Guardians.TV. "This one is special. Never gets old." While it's not known how many regulars will play Sunday for the Guardians, there's still an opportunity to head into the postseason on a serious surge. "Everybody's done their job all year, and they know what they got to do the rest of the year," Cleveland pitcher Gavin Williams also told Guardians.TV. Cleveland star Steven Kwan had three hits Saturday, and is 11-for-27 in the last seven games, but could be rested or limited for the finale. "This is so exciting," Kwan said. "This is a really fun group. ... Could be a special one, for sure." Despite no postseason ramifications for this contest, the Guardians will start Parker Messick (12-9, 2.55 ERA) in an apparent opportunity to stay sharp with the team's extended time off ahead. In 14 starts since July 4, the left-hander owns a 2.19 ERA. He allowed a run over six solid innings of Cleveland's 11-1 victory over Kansas City on Aug. 30. The Royals (68-93), meanwhile, are slated to close the season with starter Daniel Lynch IV (6-6, 4.13 ERA), who is 2-4 with a 7.01 ERA in nine starts since joining the club's injury-riddled rotation. On Tuesday, the left-hander allowed nine runs and seven hits, including three homers, while also walking three batters, over four innings against the White Sox. "I still have confidence in myself," Lynch said. "Everybody has bad starts. I just take away from it being able to move forward and flush it." Lynch yielded a two-run homer to Angel Martinez, two other hits and two walks over 3 1/3 innings of his start at Cleveland on Aug. 29. Ravaged by injuries to several key players, especially to their pitching staff, the Royals are mired in a 6-18 rut entering the final day of the regular season. They also have lost all eight of their series in September. However, rookie catcher Carter Jensen has enjoyed a breakout season. He's set to finish as Kansas City's leader in home runs (27) and RBIs (81). With two doubles Saturday, Jensen has posted a major-league rookie record 64 extra-base hits, dating to at least 1947. "He's driven. We talk about it all the time," Royals manager Matt Quatraro said of Jensen, who is batting .338 in 21 September contests. "He works, he's committed. ... He still wants to be better. He's not satisfied." With two RBI doubles Saturday, Kansas City's Jac Caglianone is 12-for-24 in his last six games. -Field Level Media

item.title: Qatar's Barshim withdraws from high jump final at Asian Games
item.description: Qatar's former world champion and Olympic gold medallist Mutaz Barshim has withdrawn from the men's high jump final at the Asian Games, the Qatar Athletics Federation said on X on Sunday, without providing further details.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Qatar's former world champion and Olympic gold medallist Mutaz Barshim has withdrawn from the men's high jump final at the Asian Games, the Qatar Athletics Federation said on X on Sunday, without providing further details. "An injury has ruled our champion Mutaz Barshim out of the men's high jump final at the Asian Games. Wishing you a speedy recovery, champion. Come back stronger," the federation said. The withdrawal is another setback for the three-time world champion, who also pulled out of the World Championships in 2025 after a foot injury disrupted his preparations despite travelling to Japan with the Qatar team. His most celebrated achievement came at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, where he shared the gold medal with Italy's Gianmarco Tamberi after both athletes cleared 2.37 metres.

item.title: Belgium’s new boss Van Bommel relishing clash with Zidane
item.description: Belgium coach Mark van Bommel is relishing the opportunity to pit his wits against Zinedine Zidane but is disappointed that Kylian Mbappe will be missing when they host France in the Nations League on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Belgium coach Mark van Bommel is relishing the opportunity to pit his wits against Zinedine Zidane but is disappointed that Kylian Mbappe will be missing when they host France in the Nations League on Monday. Van Bommel got off to a dream start in his first game in charge of Belgium with a 2-0 away win over Italy in their Group A1 game on Friday and said he wants his side to keep up the attacking approach they showed in Rome. "I started (my coaching tenure) last Monday by emphasising intensity and willingness to work," he told a press conference on Sunday. "The idea has to remain the same. Of course, you have to take the quality of the opponent into account, but that does not change our style of play. "If you are beaten in a situation, that's not a problem. As long as everyone knows what they have to do." It will also be a second game in charge for Zidane, whose [USN:L6N45H12P TEXT:"France debut on Friday"] was a 1-0 win in Turkey where goalscorer Mbappe was injured. "It is special to coach against someone like that," Van Bommel said. "He was an exceptional footballer and I played against him once, with Barca (Barcelona) against Real Madrid. If a dribbling move is named after you, then you must have done pretty well. As a coach too, of course. He is a good coach, that's clear. "I think it's a shame that Mbappe isn't there, because you always want to have the best footballers playing against you. I don't know exactly what injury he has, but I would have liked him to be there," the Belgium coach added. The France captain has since returned to Real Madrid, who said he had suffered a hyperextension of the left knee . On the eve of his debut as Belgium coach, former Dutch international Van Bommel watched his [USN:L6N45H0CH TEXT:"son Ruben debut for the Netherlands"] and set up a dramatic last-gasp equaliser against Germany in Amsterdam on Thursday. "As a father, you see your son make his debut for the Netherlands, that is already something special," Van Bommel told reporters. "We happened to be watching on the phone with a large part of the coaching staff, and then he provides an assist like that. It's fantastic. I would have liked to have been in the stadium. We then also beat Italy. It was two wonderful days."

item.title: Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers prep for playoffs in finale vs. Cards
item.description: Hard-throwing Jacob Misiorowski will get a final tuneup for the playoff-bound Milwaukee Brewers when they wrap up the regular season Sunday against the visiting St. Louis Cardinals.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Hard-throwing Jacob Misiorowski will get a final tuneup for the playoff-bound Milwaukee Brewers when they wrap up the regular season Sunday against the visiting St. Louis Cardinals. Misiorowski (15-5, 1.86 ERA), the favorite for the National League Cy Young Award, will be opposed by fellow right-hander Andre Pallante (12-8, 3.61). Misiorowski is expected to be on a limited pitch count for the second consecutive start. The Brewers (102-59) rallied to a 3-2 win over the Cardinals (77-84) on Saturday behind Brice Turang's two-run homer in the fifth inning. After starter Dustin May allowed two runs in three innings in a limited outing, the Milwaukee bullpen preserved the lead with six hitless innings. Milwaukee, which has won four consecutive NL Central division titles, has earned a first-round bye and clinched home-field advantage throughout the playoffs. The Brewers, a franchise-record 43 games over .500, have won 12 straight series at home and are 21-4-1 in home series this season. Milwaukee also had the best overall record in the majors last season before ultimately being swept by the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS. The Brewers, who have had a winning record each month this season, improved to 17-6 in September. "We were 13-13 last year in September," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after Saturday's game. "I felt like we were talking about not coasting, but what you talk about doesn't matter, it's what you do. I felt like we were beaten up a little, coasting, feeling sorry, or whatever. This team likes winning, likes achieving." Misiorowski, whose 1.86 ERA is lowest in the majors, leads the NL with 247 strikeouts, and is just one behind AL leader Gavin Williams of Cleveland. Opponents are batting just .159 against the 24-year-old Misiorowski. Misiorowski was limited to three innings in his last start, allowing just one hit, striking out four and walking none in a 44-pitch outing in a 3-0 win at Baltimore. Misiorowski is 3-1 with a 3.25 ERA in five career starts against St. Louis, including 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA with 23 strikeouts in 14 innings over two starts this season. One of the bright spots down the stretch has been Alec Burleson, who put St. Louis ahead 2-0 on Saturday with his 26th homer and third in three games. He has a majors-best 116 RBIs. "What Burley continues to do is pretty special to watch," Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol said. "It takes a lot to be as locked in for this long, and he's had a special season." Pallante has not won in six starts since his last victory against the New York Mets on Aug. 5. He is 0-2 with a 3.86 ERA in four starts in September, striking out nine and walking eight in 21 innings. Pallante was saddled with the loss in his last start, despite allowing just one run on three hits in six innings in a 2-0 setback at Pittsburgh. Pallante is 0-4 with a 6.07 ERA in 17 career games against Milwaukee, including five starts. He is 0-2 with a 9.00 ERA in two starts vs. the Brewers this season, allowing 11 runs in 11 innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: No excuses for Erasmus as Springboks beaten by Australia in Perth
item.description: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus believes his side only have themselves to blame following an epic 42-38 loss to Australia in their one-off test in Perth on Sunday, but praised the improvement of their hosts a year out from the Rugby World Cup.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus believes his side only have themselves to blame following an epic [USN:L4N45I01A TEXT:"42-38 loss to Australia"] in their one-off test in Perth on Sunday, but praised the improvement of their hosts a year out from the Rugby World Cup. Australia were full value for a 42-17 lead going into the final 10 minutes, but were reduced to an astonishing 11 players following four yellow cards in quick succession as the Springboks' pressure created ill-discipline. The visitors clawed back 21 points in that period, but ran out of time and paid the price for an error-strewn performance in the first 70 minutes of the game. "We have nobody else to blame but ourselves for the result," Erasmus told reporters. "We didn't play well enough to deserve the victory. We took a bit of a gamble with some guys who hadn't played together for a long time, but that's not an excuse. The better team won on the night." Erasmus believed the game was a valuable exercise as his side got a taste of Australia ahead of next year's World Cup and he got a look at players who had not featured in the recent 3-1 series win over New Zealand. "I know South African supporters will be upset if I sit here and say we're learning a lot while we're losing," he said. "If we'd managed to pull this game through, I would have said we'd learnt a lot about our players and how they respond in tight situations." Australia remain unbeaten under new coach Les Kiss and the Springboks coach was impressed with their improvement. "Australia don't make mistakes at the lineout, and they're always organised defensively. There are always numbers on their feet," he said. "They're a technically very well-coached team. We normally find it difficult against teams that don't miss their roles, particularly around the breakdown." He added that the influence of Australian rules football on the country's rugby side makes the Wallabies almost a unique opponent. "I think the influence of Australian rules football and rugby league is evident in their game. They're excellent in the air and they can put those contestable kicks across," Erasmus said. "They've also got those rugby league running lines where they fix defenders and create opportunities for the players around them. When they get into your 22, they're very direct and difficult to stop."

item.dc:creator: Ateeq Shariff
item.content:encoded: Gulf stock markets ended mixed on Sunday after US President Donald [USN:L6N45I003 TEXT:"Trump rejected an Iranian peace blueprint"] aimed at ending hostilities and reopening the vital Strait of Hormuz. While Tehran maintained that [USN:L6N45J004 TEXT:"diplomacy remains the only viable resolution to its conflict"] with the United States and Israel, Iran's military leadership warned that its armed forces stand fully prepared for any renewed American strikes. Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) bucked the broader unease to advance 0.8%, buoyed by strong financial sector performance. Heavyweight lenders anchored the gains. Al Rajhi Bank (1120.SE) rose 2.5% and Saudi National Bank (1180.SE) climbed 2.3%, despite weekend reports that the Saudi-led coalition had [USN:L1N45I00U TEXT:"intercepted ballistic missiles and drones"] launched toward the kingdom by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. Elsewhere, Qatar's index (.QSI) slipped 0.3%, weighed down by a 1% retreat in telecom operator Ooredoo (ORDS.QA) . Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30) slid 1.4%, pressured primarily by a 3.7% fall in tobacco monopoly Eastern Company (EAST.CA) . item.title: Jays' Max Scherzer set for finale vs. Reds, will address future later
item.description: Max Scherzer will pitch for the Toronto Blue Jays on short rest Sunday afternoon in the season finale against the visiting Cincinnati Reds.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Max Scherzer will pitch for the Toronto Blue Jays on short rest Sunday afternoon in the season finale against the visiting Cincinnati Reds. The 42-year-old right-hander stopped short, however, of saying whether this will be the final start of his Hall of Fame career. "The only thing I'll say about my future here is I'm going to make this decision about playing next year later in the offseason," Scherzer said on Saturday, prior to the Blue Jays (78-83) dropping a 5-1 decision to the Reds (75-86). "I've gone through ups and downs this season, I get it, but I've got to this point where I'm pretty healthy. I've talked to everybody in my inner circle and we all kind of feel the same way. We don't need to make a decision today. Get to the offseason and see how things unfold." Scherzer also pitched the final game of the season for Toronto last year when he was the Game 7 starter in the World Series. He did not factor into the decision in the game won by the Los Angeles Dodgers. This time he is starting the season finale between two teams playing out the schedule. "That is such a memory. Game 7 of the World Series, there is just nothing better than that," Scherzer said. "That is baseball at its pinnacle. To have the ball in that situation, competing like that and the way we played, that's just a lifelong memory." Scherzer (3-9, 6.14 ERA) is 6-2 with a 1.67 ERA in 10 career starts against the Reds. The three-time Cy Young Award winner has not faced them since 2022, however. "It will be cool facing him," said Cincinnati shortstop Elly De La Cruz, who entered the majors one year after Scherzer last faced the Reds. "He's had an incredible career," said Reds first baseman Sal Stewart, who is a favorite to be National League Rookie of the Year. "I watched him growing up. So it's really cool. He's had such a great career." Scherzer allowed four runs in five innings on Wednesday in a 4-2 road loss to the Baltimore Orioles. The Reds are scheduled to start Brandon Williamson (5-4, 4.89). The left-hander is 0-1 with a 6.35 ERA in his only career start against Toronto that came in 2023. George Springer could be playing his final game as a Blue Jay on Sunday in another possible farewell. He is at the end of a six-year contract, and manager John Schneider will try to make sure that Scherzer and Springer get the appropriate fan recognition. "That part of it is cool in an otherwise disappointing season," Schneider said. "If this is the end, hopefully it's a good sendoff." The Reds hope they have some hope for the future in the way that Rhett Lowder pitched on Saturday to finish his first complete season in the majors after his career was stalled by injuries and inconsistency. He controlled the Blue Jays through six scoreless innings. Lowder said his season was "definitely inconsistent." "I know areas I need to improve on and I'm going to improve on them," the right-hander said. "It's just good to put a full season together and know the areas I need to get better -- and I will." John Klein made his Blue Jays debut Saturday with four solid innings in relief in which he allowed two unearned runs while striking out five. --Field Level Media

item.title: Finale between Mets, Nationals focuses on individuals, not playoffs
item.description: There won't be playoff spots on the line when the visiting New York Mets and Washington Nationals conclude their season on Sunday afternoon, but there will be several players to watch.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: There won't be playoff spots on the line when the visiting New York Mets and Washington Nationals conclude their season on Sunday afternoon, but there will be several players to watch. For Washington, left-hander DJ Herz (0-1, 9.00 ERA) will make his second start since his return from Tommy John surgery as he looks to be part of the Nationals' 2027 rotation. New York outfielder Carson Benge will seek to finish an impressive weekend and continue a run at National League Rookie of the Year honors. Washington's James Wood and CJ Abrams will try to provide fireworks for the Nationals' faithful who brave the dubious weather forecast that pushed the game's first pitch from 3:05 p.m. to 1:05 p.m. ET. New York will start veteran left-hander Sean Manaea (6-7, 4.67 ERA) in the finale. Manaea, who began the year in the bullpen, has one year remaining on his three-year, $75 million contract, and that season could be spent as either a starter or a reliever. The 34-year-old is coming off a 6-3 win Tuesday against the Texas Rangers in a game in which he gave up three runs (two earned) on three hits in six innings. Manaea struck out nine and walked two. "Sean, if he takes advantage of this offseason and really gets after it, and he's back at the 94, 95 [mph] range, his stuff really, really plays," Mets manager Andy Green said. Manaea is 1-3 with a 5.48 ERA in nine career games (seven starts) vs. Washington. Herz, 25, made his first start since 2024 on Monday in a 9-2 loss to the Detroit Tigers and gave up four runs on five hits over four innings. "You definitely have to flip that switch [out of rehab mode]," he said. "... Getting that first one under the belt again, there were a lot of good moments that I feel were DJ Herz, and then there are some moments that we need to get a little bit better at. We'll figure it out." Herz is 0-2 with an 8.31 ERA in three career appearances vs. the Mets. On Saturday, rookie A.J. Ewing hit a three-run homer and Ronny Mauricio hit a pair of home runs in New York's 7-1 win. Benge, 23, had three hits, including a double, and made a highlight-reel diving catch in right center. Over his last nine games, he is hitting .441 with two home runs, six RBIs and seven runs. He has multiple hits in six of his last 12 games and raised his season batting average to .280. "I feel like that (Rookie of the Year) is a huge award, and there's a bunch of guys in the running -- one being [pitcher Nolan McLean] in this clubhouse," Benge said of the honor. "But I feel like there's a lot of good players in there, and winning that would be amazing." New York's Juan Soto was hit on the right hand by a pitch in the ninth inning. He left the game, but X-rays were negative. The highlight for Washington was three scoreless innings by left-hander Connelly Early -- obtained from the Boston Red Sox in July while on the injured list -- in his Nationals debut. "I thought he looked really good," Washington manager Blake Butera said. "He attacked hitters, he wasn't afraid, [he] threw a ton of strikes. I was happy with the performance." Wood had two hits for Washington. He needs one homer to match his career high of 31. Abrams will look to add to his career-high totals in home run (33) and RBIs (105). --Field Level Media

item.title: World T20 champions India on alert for Afghanistan after Japan scare
item.description: India captain Shreyas Iyer ruled out any complacency ahead of Monday's Asian Games quarter-finals against Afghanistan, conceding last week's scare against Japan had jolted the Twenty20 world champions out of any complacence.
item.dc:creator: Amlan Chakraborty
item.content:encoded: India captain Shreyas Iyer ruled out any complacency ahead of Monday's Asian Games quarter-finals against Afghanistan, conceding last week's scare against Japan had jolted the Twenty20 world champions out of any complacence. In a rain-hit match at Sano, India edged Japan in a five-over shootout to lift the Suzuki Cup in the maiden one-off meeting between the men's sides — [USN:L6N45E03C TEXT:"a jolt"] that underlined the danger of underestimating any opponent in alien conditions. India, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Sri Lanka are seeded directly into the last eight, while Nepal, Afghanistan, Malaysia and Hong Kong advanced from the preliminary groups. With India's women having [USN:L6N45E03V TEXT:"successfully defended"] their Asian Games title, attention now turns to Iyer's side to emulate them. "Not just Afghanistan, no team can be taken lightly at any stage - just look at how tough Japan made it for us the other day," Iyer said on Sunday. "The pitches here cannot be set to a certain standard, so to adapt is key. It will be challenging for all the teams." Expectation remains sky-high for the sport's most followed team, and Iyer acknowledged the scrutiny that comes with the jersey. "Whenever you represent India, there are a lot of expectations, that you have to finish at the top. That is always there," Iyer said of the "good pressure". "When there are expectations, you want to deliver. But I think we shouldn't think of the outcome too much. We have set a standard as a team, and we must try to transcend that in every match." Preparation has been complicated by persistent rain at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, limiting India to only light work on Sunday, with the forecast uncertain for match day. "We have to be mentally prepared irrespective of whatever the situation is going to be. We did get a decent chance to warm up and knock the ball around today, and now the task is to adapt quickly to the pitch," he said. In Monday's other action, Pakistan face Hong Kong in the first quarter-final.

item.title: Trump dice detenidos en base aérea británica utilizada por EEUU pretendían causar "grandes daños"
item.description: La policía británica detuvo el domingo a cinco hombres como sospechosos de delitos relacionados con explosivos y terrorismo cerca de una base aérea que ha sido utilizada por Estados Unidos para lanzar ataques contra Irán, tras recibir un aviso de que se habían visto tres furgonetas dirigiéndose hacia el aeródromo militar.
item.dc:creator: Toby Shepheard
item.content:encoded: La policía británica detuvo el domingo a cinco hombres como sospechosos de delitos relacionados con explosivos y terrorismo cerca de una base aérea que ha sido utilizada por Estados Unidos para lanzar ataques contra Irán, tras recibir un aviso de que se habían visto tres furgonetas dirigiéndose hacia el aeródromo militar. El presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, afirmó que los sospechosos pretendían causar "grandes daños" y que estaban siendo investigados por las autoridades británicas y estadounidenses. Los agentes antiterroristas británicos que dirigen la investigación indicaron que la policía había recibido una llamada sobre tres vehículos sospechosos que parecían dirigirse hacia la base aérea de la RAF en Fairford, al oeste de Inglaterra, en la madrugada del domingo. Cinco hombres fueron detenidos por agentes armados y posteriormente puestos bajo custodia como sospechosos de preparar un acto terrorista. La policía, que afirmó creer que el incidente ya estaba controlado, aún no ha revelado públicamente quiénes son, según su valoración, los implicados. Se considera más probable que el motivo esté relacionado con Irán, según una fuente cercana a la investigación, aunque también se barajan la posibilidad de una operación de sabotaje rusa o un complot islamista. LA POLICÍA TRABAJA PARA ACLARAR LAS CIRCUNSTANCIAS "Nos encontramos en las primeras fases de la investigación y cinco hombres permanecen detenidos", declaró en un comunicado la coordinadora nacional principal de la Policía Antiterrorista, Vicki Evans. "Como es de esperar, estamos colaborando estrechamente con nuestros socios para esclarecer las circunstancias del incidente". La policía informó que se había establecido un cordón de seguridad de 400 metros alrededor de la base mientras la unidad de desactivación de explosivos inspeccionaba las furgonetas. Se evacuó a los residentes de 85 viviendas de un pueblo cercano y agentes armados patrullaban la zona. El Gobierno británico, que ha autorizado a Estados Unidos a utilizar bombarderos con base en Fairford para atacar instalaciones de misiles iraníes que estaban atacando buques en el estrecho de Ormuz, señaló que el primer ministro, Andy Burnham, estaba siendo informado sobre el incidente. Burnham agradeció a la policía y a las fuerzas armadas. "Sé que el incidente de hoy cerca de la base de la RAF en Fairford será motivo de gran preocupación para los residentes locales y para muchas personas que siguen la evolución de los acontecimientos en todo el país", dijo en X. Reino Unido declaró en julio que sus fuerzas armadas estaban preparadas para proteger al país de cualquier ataque después de que la Guardia Revolucionaria iraní le advirtiera que no permitiera que los bombarderos estadounidenses volaran desde Fairford, afirmando que cualquier base utilizada para lanzar ataques sería un objetivo legítimo. "La detención en el Reino Unido fue fantástica", declaró Trump a periodistas, calificándola de "un trabajo increíble". "Los teníamos bajo investigación. Pretendían causar un gran daño a nuestra fortaleza y la colaboración con los británicos funcionó de maravilla. Los teníamos bajo vigilancia desde hacía mucho tiempo y los hemos capturado", añadió Trump. El domingo por la mañana la base quedó bloqueada por policías armados, mientras que maquinaria pesada impedía también el acceso; además, testigos de Reuters indicaron que se había reforzado la seguridad en otras bases utilizadas por Estados Unidos, con vehículos blindados y soldados en las entradas de la RAF Lakenheath y la RAF Mildenhall, en el este de Inglaterra. DECLARACIÓN DE INCIDENTE GRAVE Una agricultora de la zona contó al periódico Daily Telegraph que había alertado a la policía tras ver las furgonetas y a unos hombres actuando de forma sospechosa mientras conducía de vuelta a casa tras una fiesta. "Vi a un grupo de jóvenes de aspecto de Oriente Medio corriendo entre los árboles. Algunos llevaban máscaras o pasamontañas, y todos se dispersaron delante de nosotros mientras pasábamos de nuevo con el coche", declaró al periódico. "Algunos se adentraron en los campos y otros giraron para correr hacia la base aérea… Es decir, uno no ve a hombres enmascarados corriendo a la una y media de la madrugada en el campo, cerca de una base aérea de alta seguridad, sin preocuparse". El concejal Tristan Wilkinson declaró a Reuters que recientemente se había producido una alerta de seguridad en Fairford y que se había reforzado la vigilancia. "Hubo una amenaza concreta hace unas seis semanas por parte de los iraníes contra esta base. En aquel momento, se intensificó la vigilancia en los alrededores", afirmó. Un portavoz de la Fuerza Aérea de Estados Unidos se negó a comentar las medidas específicas de protección de las fuerzas en la base. "La 501.ª Ala de Apoyo al Combate y nuestras demás alas con base en el Reino Unido permanecen en alerta y tomarán las medidas adecuadas para garantizar la seguridad de nuestros militares estadounidenses, civiles, contratistas y sus familias", afirmó el portavoz. Los ministros británicos también han informado previamente a los gestores de infraestructuras críticas sobre la amenaza que supone Rusia, y el Gobierno está cada vez más preocupado por posibles operaciones de sabotaje y ciberataques. Rusia niega estar lanzando ataques híbridos contra países occidentales.

item.title: Inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra cobran 56 vidas en la India y 14 en Nepal
item.description: Las fuertes lluvias y tormentas han provocado inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra que han causado la muerte de 56 personas en la India, mientras que en Nepal han fallecido 14 personas y otras 11 están desaparecidas.
item.dc:creator: Jatindra Dash, Gopal Sharma
item.content:encoded: Las fuertes lluvias y tormentas han provocado inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra que han causado la muerte de 56 personas en la India, mientras que en Nepal han fallecido 14 personas y otras 11 están desaparecidas. En Nepal, las autoridades advirtieron el domingo que podrían producirse más crecidas repentinas. El estado de Uttar Pradesh, en el norte de la India, registró 66,5 mm de lluvia entre el 25 de septiembre y la mañana del 27 de septiembre, frente a los 7,6 mm habituales para ese periodo, según declaró el domingo Hrishikesh Bhaskar Yashod, comisario de ayuda humanitaria del estado. Las autoridades están llevando a cabo operaciones de rescate en las zonas anegadas y distribuyendo ayuda humanitaria, mientras que se ha ordenado a los funcionarios que evalúen los daños en los cultivos y proporcionen indemnizaciones. Además de las 56 víctimas mortales, 46 personas han resultado heridas y más de 1.000 viviendas han sufrido daños. Las autoridades nepalíes advirtieron de posibles crecidas repentinas en 49 de los 77 distritos del país, y más de la mitad de ellos se enfrentan a un alto riesgo de inundaciones o crecidas repentinas, ya que los niveles de agua en los principales ríos y afluentes siguen subiendo. Shanti Mahat, portavoz de la Autoridad Nacional para la Reducción y Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres, afirmó que Rasuwa y Nuwakot —zonas afectadas por las mortíferas inundaciones del mes pasado, que se cobraron la vida de más de 1.450 personas y dejaron a miles de desaparecidos— deben permanecer "en alerta", aunque actualmente no se consideran zonas de alto riesgo. El suministro eléctrico se ha interrumpido por completo en los distritos de Manang, Mustang, Myagdi y Baglung, y las autoridades están trabajando para restablecer la electricidad, según informaron responsables del ministerio de Energía. La crecida del río Rahuganga ha dañado la estructura y las torres de las líneas de transmisión de una central hidroeléctrica de 40 megavatios, según ha declarado el ministro de Recursos Hídricos y Energía, Biraj Bhakta Shrestha. En la India, la Comisión Central del Agua señaló que 30 estaciones de control fluvial repartidas por siete estados indicaban una "situación grave". Varios ríos importantes, entre ellos el Ganges, el Gandak, el Kosi, el Bagmati y el Narmada, superaban los niveles de peligro. Las inundaciones y los deslizamientos de tierra también interrumpieron las telecomunicaciones en algunas zonas de Nepal tras los daños sufridos por las fibras ópticas y el suministro eléctrico, según declaró el ministro de Comunicaciones, Bikram Timilsinha. En otro incidente ocurrido en Nepal, diez trabajadores locales también se encontraban desaparecidos después de que una avalancha sepultara el campamento base del Himlung Himal, de 7.126 metros, en el distrito septentrional de Manang, según informaron responsables de senderismo. Los trabajadores estaban montando tiendas de campaña para escaladores extranjeros, que no se encontraban allí cuando se produjo la avalancha.

item.title: Thai trailblazer claims Asian Games sprint double in rainy Nagoya
item.description: Puripol Boonson stormed to the 200-meter gold on a damp track to complete the Asian Games sprint double while China's javelin sensation Yan Ziyi defeated an Olympic champion.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: Puripol Boonson broke new ground for Thailand athletics on Sunday, storming to the 200 metres gold on a damp track to complete the Asian Games sprint double while China's javelin sensation Yan Ziyi defeated an Olympic champion. Having claimed the [USN:L1N45H0A1 TEXT:"100m gold in 9.90 seconds"] two days ago, 20-year-old Puripol became the first Thai sprinter to break the 20-second barrier in the 200m with a run of 19.88. His time at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium matched the seven-year-old Asian record set by China's Xie Zhenye and confirmed him as one of the continent's most exciting track talents ahead of next year's world championships in Beijing. "I'm going to aim for more golds and more records. I can't say how fast it's going to be, but it's going to be more records and faster," said Puripol, who was more than a half-second quicker than China's runner-up Huang Youwen. Puripol was one of several young guns firing at the track and field. Yan, 18, who has taken the athletics world by storm in her debut season this year, needed only one throw of 70.46 to beat Olympic champion and home hero Haruka Kitaguchi (62.70) for her first Asian Games gold. One of athletics' biggest drawcards was lost when former Olympic champion Mutaz Barshim pulled out of the high jump due to injury, leaving Taiwan's Fu Chao-hsuan to take the title (2.25m). Bahrain's Olympic champion Winfred Yavi cruised to the 3,000m steeplechase title in 9:04.36, adding to her 10,000m gold, while Singapore's Shanti Pereira retained the women's 200m title in 22.78, becoming the first to win the event back-to-back. Beaten by China's rising star Chen Yujie for the 100m gold, Pereira denied the 17-year-old by 0.15 seconds in the 200m. "I was like, ’No, you (Chen) got it that day. Today is me. Nothing in the world is going (to) stop me'," said the 30-year-old. CRAMPED ATHLETES Five years after Japan staged an Olympics without fans due to COVID-19 restrictions, the Aichi-Nagoya Games have been under scrutiny over a lack of fan interest, and rainy weather proved a dampener on the eighth full day, with banks of empty seats at competition venues. Accommodation has also been in the spotlight, with organisers opting to house athletes and officials in a mix of hotels, temporary wooden huts and a cruise ship. Some athletes had found them [USN:L6N45J02M TEXT:""rather cramped", an official admitted"]. South Korea beat hosts Japan 3-1 in a battle of Asia's baseball powers for the men's gold, while squash powerhouse Malaysia celebrated as Ng Eain Yow and Sivasangari Subramaniam won back-to-back gold in the men's and women's singles respectively. The Malaysian duo became the first athletes to earn quota berths to the sport's Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028. Subramaniam, who has gone from strength to strength since [USN:L6N45J027 TEXT:"a near-fatal crash"] in 2022, said: "World number one and an Olympic gold medal is my goal." Sunday kicked off with penalty-laden race walk events, with India's Priyanka Goswami, a Commonwealth Games runner-up, disqualified for racking up too many red cards in the women's marathon, which was won by Kazakh Yasmina Toxanbayeva. World bronze medallist Hayato Katsuki walked "cautiously" to win the men's marathon gold for Japan in 3:03:36, leaving a three-minute gap to China's runner-up Zhou Yingcheng. "I’m confident that in terms of power, I’m the best in the world," said the 35-year-old, who won his second Games title after the 50-km gold at Jakarta 2018.

item.title: Czechs down Ukraine to claim 12th Billie Jean King Cup crown
item.description: Czech Republic brushed aside Ukraine to win their 12th Billie Jean King Cup title in Shenzhen, China, on Sunday, with Karolina Muchova and Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova delivering an unassailable 2-0 lead in the final.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Czech Republic brushed aside Ukraine to win their 12th Billie Jean King Cup title in Shenzhen, China, on Sunday, with Karolina Muchova and Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova delivering an unassailable 2-0 lead in the final. Wimbledon runner-up Muchova swept past Anhelina Kalinina 6-2 6-3 in the opening singles rubber before Noskova toppled world number seven Elina Svitolina 6-3 7-6(5) to seal the title. The Czechs are the second-most successful nation in the history of the premier international women's team competition, behind the United States, who hold a record 18 titles. Ukraine were seeking their first Billie Jean King Cup crown. "It's very special," Muchova said. "A dream of mine to lift the trophy. To do it with these girls sitting here, it's a pleasure. "I'm just so proud of us - how we manage whole week, how we fight, how we practice whole week, how we just have the vibe in the locker room. It was such a nice time. "To win it is like a cherry on the top. I'm just so grateful it happened, that we can celebrate now." Muchova laid the foundations for victory with a dominant serving performance, firing eight aces and winning 86% of points behind her first serve. The world number eight did not face a break point and converted four of her five break-point opportunities during the 70-minute contest. Noskova was tested more sternly by Svitolina but the 21-year-old produced another composed display, striking 10 aces and holding firm in a tense second set to complete the title-clinching victory in one hour and 33 minutes. Katerina Siniakova, a 12-time Grand Slam women's doubles champion, had been named alongside Marie Bouzkova for the doubles rubber, but the Czech Republic wrapped up the tie in the singles to seal their first Billie Jean King Cup title since 2018. Ukraine had [USN:L4N45I03H TEXT:"stunned two-time defending champions Italy"] in the semi-finals to reach their first Billie Jean King Cup final, while the Czech Republic advanced to their first title decider since 2018 [USN:L4N45H0P9 TEXT:"by beating Spain"]. The Billie Jean King Cup began in 1963 as the Federation Cup, launched by the International Tennis Federation to mark its 50th anniversary and conceived as the women's equivalent of the Davis Cup. The inaugural tournament, featuring 16 nations, was staged at Queen's Club in London, where the United States - with Billie Jean King, then Billie Jean Moffitt, in the team - beat Australia in the final. The competition was shortened to the Fed Cup in 1995, when its format was overhauled to introduce home-and-away ties. It retained that name until 2020, when it was renamed the Billie Jean King Cup in honour of King, who won the competition seven times as a player and four times as captain, including once as player-captain. The rebranding also coincided with another restructuring of the competition around a central Finals event.

item.title: León insta a la Iglesia a asumir sus fallas antes de reunirse con supervivientes de abusos en Francia
item.description: El papa León instó el domingo a la Iglesia católica a reconocer sus propios errores y a sanar las "heridas profundas" infligidas en su seno, horas antes de reunirse con víctimas de abusos a menores por parte de sacerdotes en Francia.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: El papa León instó el domingo a la Iglesia católica a reconocer sus propios errores y a sanar las "heridas profundas" infligidas en su seno, horas antes de reunirse con víctimas de abusos a menores por parte de sacerdotes en Francia. León, dirigiéndose a una multitud que se extendía por un amplio prado cercano al famoso santuario católico de Lourdes, afirmó que la Iglesia debe tener el valor de afrontar su pasado, aunque no hizo referencia directa a los escándalos de abusos en Francia que han conmocionado a todo el país. "Para sanar las profundas heridas, las infidelidades y los dolorosos errores que se han producido en el seno de (la Iglesia), debemos someternos humildemente a la mirada purificadora del Señor", declaró el primer papa estadounidense ante unas 150.000 personas reunidas en el prado en un día soleado. León está en una visita de cuatro días por tres ciudades de Francia, donde ha instado de nuevo al mundo a reconsiderar el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial. El sábado reunió a unas 800.000 personas en una misa al aire libre celebrada en los Campos Elíseos de París. Los responsables de la Iglesia local esperan que ayude a restaurar la reputación de la Iglesia después de que un informe de 2021 revelara que unos 330.000 niños franceses habían sufrido abusos por parte del clero católico y de líderes laicos a lo largo de siete décadas. En una reunión a puerta cerrada celebrada el domingo con los obispos franceses, León se refirió directamente a "el doloroso flagelo de los abusos cometidos contra menores por miembros del clero", según un texto facilitado por el Vaticano. El papa agradeció a los obispos las "medidas valientes" que, según él, habían tomado para hacer frente a los escándalos y les instó a reforzar sus esfuerzos de protección y a "continuar por el camino emprendido, manteniendo la máxima vigilancia". VÍCTIMAS SE MUESTRAN ESCÉPTICAS León ya se había disculpado anteriormente de forma directa por los escándalos de abusos que han dañado la credibilidad de la Iglesia en todo el mundo. En un viaje a España en junio, dijo a los obispos de allí que debían escuchar a los supervivientes y ofrecerles reparaciones. El papa tiene previsto mantener este domingo, a última hora, una reunión a puerta cerrada con siete víctimas francesas de abusos por parte del clero. Algunos supervivientes se mostraron escépticos respecto a que el encuentro dé lugar a cambios rápidos por parte de la Iglesia. "Soy bastante escéptica respecto a que el papa vaya a resolver el problema, al menos no de forma inmediata", declaró a Reuters Michèle Le Reun-Gaigné, copresidenta de una asociación de supervivientes del oeste de Francia. "Las cosas avanzan muy lentamente. No va a suceder de la noche a la mañana". El obispo Pierre-Antoine Bozo, portavoz de los obispos franceses, señaló que el deseo del papa de celebrar la reunión "demuestra que no podemos ignorar este asunto y que debe seguir figurando siempre entre nuestras preocupaciones". LOURDES, VINCULADA AL ESCÁNDALO DEL VATICANO El itinerario del papa en Francia incluye seis actos en Lourdes, una localidad situada en las estribaciones de los Pirineos que atrae a unos tres millones de peregrinos al año para visitar un santuario dedicado a la Virgen María y unas aguas termales a las que se atribuyen propiedades curativas. El lugar también está relacionado con un escándalo que ha acosado al Vaticano en los últimos años. La fachada del santuario cuenta con una serie de mosaicos del reverendo Marko Rupnik, un destacado artista religioso vinculado al Vaticano, que ha sido acusado de abusos sexuales. Rupnik, acusado por más de 20 mujeres, no se sabe que haya hecho comentarios públicos sobre las acusaciones. Cinco de sus presuntas víctimas escribieron el jueves una carta abierta al papa en la que criticaban duramente el juicio que el Vaticano está llevando a cabo contra el clérigo. Los mosaicos, de varias plantas de altura, han sido cubiertos para la visita del papa con grandes lonas de color amarillo apagado. Al llegar para la misa del domingo, León fue conducido en su papamóvil descapotable cerca de la fachada del santuario y de los mosaicos cubiertos. El papa, que el viernes reiteró con firmeza la oposición católica a las iniciativas de muerte asistida dos meses después de que Francia estableciera el derecho legal a morir para las personas con enfermedades incurables, volvió a mencionar en Lourdes la postura provida de la Iglesia. Afirmó que la acogida que brinda el santuario a los peregrinos enfermos que esperan encontrar un milagro en sus aguas se opone a "las tendencias actuales que pretenden redefinir el valor de la vida humana ante la enfermedad".

item.title: Organisers fend off bed-size complaints in Nagoya
item.description: It was never going to be a bed of roses when container-style blocks were used to house athletes, but Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games organisers said using ottomans as extensions could have brought more comfort to taller competitors.
item.dc:creator: Amlan Chakraborty, Irene Wang
item.content:encoded: It was never going to be a bed of roses when container-style blocks were used to house athletes, but Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games organisers said using ottomans as extensions could have brought more comfort to taller competitors. Complaints about cramped rooms and small beds surfaced on social media from athletes staying in the modular units, adding to the woes of the organisers, who have drawn flak for not building a traditional Athletes' Village. On Sunday, media were given a peek inside the container-style athletes' accommodation at the Garden Pier that looked like a minimalist Lego city. The wood-lined rooms looked compact and the beds appeared short — especially for typically tall basketball players — though a separate, spacious dining hall and a shop selling basic necessities aimed to offset the squeeze. South Korea have already moved their men's basketball team into standard hotels, but Yuta Matsuo, deputy director of the Games' athlete accommodation section, and his team braved rain to explain the "sustainable" rationale behind the setup. "The most requests we have received was about the size of the bed, particularly from the basketball players and other athletes with larger physiques," Matsuo told reporters. "When there were more beds and more people staying in the rooms, they felt the space was rather cramped. "We had thought that the bed extension, ottomans, could be used effectively to make better use of the available space. However, we could have done a better job of explaining how these tools could be used, because they may not have been used as effectively as we had hoped. "Going forward, we would like to improve the way we communicate what these items are for and how they can be used, so that we can provide the athletes with a more comfortable environment during their stay." The organisers are also using a cruise ship and hotels to accommodate 17,000 athletes and officials who have descended on the port city. "It is becoming increasingly difficult in Japan to develop entirely new facilities," Matsuo said, referring to the absence of a dedicated Athletes' Village. "So in terms of how to make the most effective use of existing facilities while ensuring that they properly meet the needs of the athletes, we hope to continue making improvements in these areas." Coach of the Mongolian women's basketball team Javier Garcia Alvarez has been critical of the accommodations. "Especially for basketball players who are like 185, 190 centimetres, it's not easy," Alvarez told Reuters. "When you are coming to these villages and they are like this, I mean, you have to adapt to this. It's almost like camping, it's like a camp." India used similar units for some of their athletes [USN:L6N44W0XB TEXT:"to acclimatise"] for the continental showpiece.

item.title: Australia hold on to beat South Africa with 11 men in Perth
item.description: Australia held on with 11 men in a dramatic finish to beat a second-string South Africa outfit 42-38 at Perth Stadium on Sunday and extend their unbeaten run to five games since new coach Les Kiss took over in late July.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia held on with 11 men in a dramatic finish to beat a second-string South Africa outfit 42-38 at Perth Stadium on Sunday and extend their unbeaten run to five games since new coach Les Kiss took over in late July. Skipper Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan, Joseph Suaalii and Hunter Paisami were all shown yellow cards in the last 10 minutes as the world champions cut a 25-point deficit down to four at the final whistle. Australia had looked to be cruising after centre Len Ikitau's double and tries from flyhalf Ben Donaldson, number eight Wilson and winger Max Jorgensen combined with 17 points from the boot of scrumhalf Ryan Lonergan gave them a 42-17 lead after 65 minutes. The last 10 minutes threatened to undo all their earlier good work but the Wallabies will move on to back-to-back tests against the All Blacks in October without a loss in six games, their best unbeaten run since 2017. "I'm so proud of the group," said Wilson. "We versed the world champions in our own backyard here. Jeez, that was a crazy last 10 minutes, but that first 70 minutes, the way we played, we implemented our game plan in exactly the way we wanted." South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus had made 13 changes to his lineup from the team which completed the gruelling 3-1 series victory over New Zealand earlier this month but stacked his bench with first-choice players as an insurance policy. It almost paid off in the frantic last 10 minutes, but scores from hooker Johan Grobbelaar, winger Edwill van der Merwe, scrumhalf Morne van den Berg, prop Ox Nche as well as a penalty try were not quite enough. "Australia is always a hard team to beat, and such a good game to play," said Springboks captain Andre Esterhuizen. "It was a pretty intense game and quite quick for a test match, but they capitalised on all our errors, and I think discipline let us down, especially in that first half." The visitors scored the first try after Handre Pollard and Lonergan had exchanged early penalties with Grobbelaar rolling over the line on the back of a rolling maul. Australia responded with two tries from Ikitau in three minutes, the first from close range and the second after winger Suaalii had disrupted the restart and the ball bounced back to the lurking centre. The Springboks responded almost immediately to lock up the scores again at 17-17, flyhalf Pollard's long pass exposing a hole in the Australian backline defence and Van der Merwe showing his pace to finish the move. A slanted crosskick from Wallabies fullback Tom Wright gave Jorgensen some space to run shortly before halftime, however, and Australia recycled patiently when the winger was held up shy of the line with Donaldson going over unopposed in the corner after 14 phases. Lonergan extended Australia's lead with his second penalty eight minutes into the second half, prompting Erasmus to bring on all eight of his replacements, and added a third three-pointer after 54 minutes to make it 30-17. The Wallabies were now taking the Springboks on up front and tapped a penalty close to the line just before the hour mark with Wilson forcing his way over and slapping the ball down for a try. The Springboks stormed back to try and cut the 20-point deficit but when Canan Moodie spilled the ball, Jorgensen was on hand to scoop it up and sprint 60 metres for Australia's fifth try.

item.title: Free-falling Phillies keep playoff berth in sight in finale vs. Rays
item.description: Once a virtual lock to make the playoffs, the Philadelphia Phillies will enter the final day of the regular season with their postseason hopes still up in the air.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Once a virtual lock to make the playoffs, the Philadelphia Phillies will enter the final day of the regular season with their postseason hopes still up in the air. The Phillies (87-74) can clinch their fifth straight postseason berth on Sunday afternoon when they host the American League East champion Tampa Bay Rays (98-63) in the regular-season finale for both teams. Right-hander Zack Wheeler (13-5, 3.06 ERA) will try to rescue the Phillies, who have lost four games in a row, all on nights in which they could have clinched a National League wild-card berth. Philadelphia not only lost each of those contests, but the Arizona Diamondbacks (86-75) -- the Phillies' lone remaining competition for the NL's final playoff spot -- have been hot for the past week. Arizona had won six straight games before falling 10-7 to the San Diego Padres on Saturday. That brought Philadelphia's magic number to one heading into Game 162. In four starts this month, Wheeler is 2-0 with a 1.75 ERA. He struck out 11 batters in 5 2/3 innings against the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday in his last start, allowing three runs and five hits in a no-decision in the Phillies' 6-4 victory. "I feel like he's getting better every time out," Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said of Wheeler, who struck out the first seven Brewers he faced and crossed the 2,000-strikeout plateau for his career. Wheeler has faced the Rays five times in his career, going 2-2 with a 4.11 ERA. "We're always confident when that guy's on the mound," catcher J.T. Realmuto said after Saturday's setback. Tampa Bay will start right-hander Nick Martinez (15-5, 2.94 ERA), who gave up two runs over six innings in a 2-0 loss to the New York Yankees on Tuesday in his most recent outing. Martinez struck out a season-high seven batters but still suffered his first loss in more than a month, giving up a two-run homer to Cody Bellinger in the fourth inning after Ben Rice had doubled. "Two pitches that leaked back over the plate, and they were back-to-back pitches," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "But Nick did everything else really, really incredibly well, as usual." Martinez is 0-1 with a 3.31 ERA in six lifetime games (one start) against the Phillies. On Sunday, he will face a lineup that has a total of three runs over the last four games. "You might think I'm crazy, but tonight ... our guys fought the whole way," Mattingly said following Saturday's 12-1 loss to the Rays. "... I was actually encouraged at the end of that game. Maybe I'm being overly optimistic, but I was encouraged tonight." Richie Palacios drove in four runs, and Victor Mesa Jr. had four hits and two RBIs to highlight Saturday's win for Tampa Bay. Other standouts for the Rays included Junior Caminero, who slugged his 42nd homer, and Yandy Diaz, who collected three hits and scored three runs. Caminero, who is expected to finish in the top five of the American League MVP voting, will complete his 162-game season when he takes the field Sunday. "It's amazing. What a feat," Martinez said. Caminero and the Rays already have earned a first-round bye in the playoffs and will face the winner of the wild-card series between the Yankees and Boston Red Sox. "We keep fighting every single day," Caminero said. "Every game matters for us." --Field Level Media

item.title: Barrick Mining reaches deal with unions at Mali gold mine, easing strike threat
item.description: Canada's Barrick Mining has signed a new collective bargaining agreement with unions representing workers at its Loulo-Gounkoto gold mine in western Mali, a company spokesperson and a union official said on Sunday, easing the threat of a strike.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada's Barrick Mining (ABX.TO) has signed a new collective bargaining agreement with unions representing workers at its Loulo-Gounkoto gold mine in western Mali, a company spokesperson and a union official said on Sunday, easing the threat of a strike. "We confirm that we have signed a new Collective Bargaining Agreement with the LG unions," the spokesperson said. Bani Sacko, a union official at Barrick's Loulo-Gounkoto complex, confirmed to Reuters on phone call that strike action has been called off. "On Monday the 21st, after a meeting, an agreement was reached and the strike action has since been called off. Apparently, all the other strike actions have also been called off," Sacko said. The Loulo-Gounkoto unions had submitted a list of 15 demands, Sacko added. The agreement was earlier reported by Bloomberg News, which cited Abdoulaye Coulibaly of Mali's National Union of Malian Workers. "The strike threat has been resolved," Coulibaly said, according to the Bloomberg report. He added that the agreement involved workers at Food & Events Africa, Somilo SA and Gounkoto SA. Earlier this month, unions representing workers at Somilo and Gounkoto [USN:L8N45A1JK TEXT:"said they would"] begin strike action at the end of September unless demands on overtime pay, reimbursement of mission expenses and implementation of labour agreements were met. Separate strike notices were also submitted by Barrick's catering and support staff contractor Food & Events Africa as well as workers in Mali's mining regulator and other mining administration agencies. Mali, one of Africa's leading gold producers, [USN:L8N3Z92IN TEXT:"resolved a dispute"] with Barrick in November last year over profit-sharing and control of the Loulo-Gounkoto gold mining complex after two years of negotiations. Toronto-based Barrick temporarily [USN:L4N3X0128 TEXT:"suspended operations"] in January last year, after Mali's military-led authorities arrested the miner's employees and issued an arrest warrant for the company's former CEO Mark Bristow for alleged financial crimes. The Malian government [USN:L8N43Q102 TEXT:"tightened its grip"] on the mining sector under a 2023 mining code aimed at boosting state revenues from the country's natural resources.

item.content:encoded: Le groupe de luxe italien Armani est disposé à envisager plusieurs investisseurs pour la vente d'une participation de 15% prévue dans le testament du fondateur Giorgio Armani, a déclaré dimanche son directeur général, Giuseppe Marsocci. "Il n’est pas gravé dans le marbre qu’il doive s’agir d’un seul investisseur", a déclaré Giuseppe Marsocci aux journalistes en marge du défilé Giorgio Armani, ajoutant qu’aucune décision n’avait encore été prise.
